To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
'the X-ray spectrum is the most important single diagnostic tool available for classifying active galactic nuclei, and that the 0.1--0.4 kev band is the most useful for this purpose'.
the 0.1–0.4 ke V band is a very effective way of finding NLS1s and that a steep X- ray spectrum is a better predictor of an 'extremely active' nucleus than a narrow Hβ linewidth.

(1) the fraction of Seyferts with X-ray spectra as steep as those of NLS1s is ∼40 per cent, (2) the fraction of NLS1 galaxies is ∼10 per cent of the total Seyfert population and (3) the space density of steep-spectrum Seyferts is comparable with that of the NLS1 galaxies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the properties of a complete sample of X-ray-selected Seyfert nuclei, which are found to be dominated by NLS1s.
the physical properties of a complete sample of 54 Seyfer galaxies, 20 of which are narrow-line Seyferts.
the properties of Seyfert-type nuclei and their relation to X-ray and optical properties of their host galaxies.
